notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.40_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.40.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.40.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Fixed

- **The app can no longer sit on "Loading…" for ever.** Starting up meant
  twelve requests to the part of Ruze that holds your account, your servers and
  your messages — each waited for in turn, and not one of them with a time
  limit on it. If a single one never answered, the loading screen stayed there:
  no error, no way to try again, and nothing said about what it was waiting
  for. A phone was the most likely to hit it, because everything it asks for
  queues behind whatever catching-up is already going on, and a phone coming
  back after a day away has the most to catch up on. The window now waits only
  for what it cannot draw without — which platform it is on, your account, your
  servers and the shape of the window. Each of those gives up after twenty
  seconds and says which one stalled, with a Try again button under it.
  Everything else — your status, your volumes, the friends list, what there is
  to discover — now arrives behind a window that is already on screen.

- **A device no longer goes straight back to a route it has just found dead.**
  Ruze chooses how to reach another device by which path is answering, and
  moves to a relay when a direct one goes quiet. What went wrong was what
  happened next: leaving a path makes the layer underneath close it, and
  closing it threw away the record of it having failed — so the same address
  looked untried a moment later, sending moved back onto it, went quiet again,
  and moved off again. Measured on a phone at forty-two seconds a lap. What a
  route did is now remembered against the route rather than against the
  connection that proved it: one caught not answering is left alone for half a
  minute, longer each time it fails again, and allowed back the moment it
  actually answers. This is one cause of a device that receives messages and
  cannot send them, and not necessarily the only one.

- **Opening the app no longer goes looking for people you have not met.** It
  used to reach for the card of every friend of every friend and take up the
  ones it had not seen — as many as forty of them — before drawing anything at
  all. That was the slowest thing in the startup and the most likely to be the
  one that never finished. It happens when you open Discover now, which is the
  screen that asks the question.
